neighbours.label: ' on' right after a form of 'sit' (sitting on the couch, sat on the bench, sits on the board); 'on' after other verbs or in time / dependence uses is quiet. Also fires on ' unto'
fire: We found her sitting on the kitchen floor with the puppy.
The old man sat on the steps and smoked his pipe.
He has agreed to sit on the hiring committee next term.
Two crows were sitting on the telephone wire outside.
My aunt sits on the board of a local charity.
The kids sat on the curb eating ice cream.
Nobody wanted to sit on the broken chair in the corner.
She was sitting on a suitcase at the bus stop.
quiet: We found her asleep on the kitchen floor with the puppy.
The old man slipped on the steps and dropped his pipe.
He has agreed to speak on the hiring process next term.
Two crows were fighting over the telephone wire outside.
My aunt relies on the staff of a local charity.
The kids dropped ice cream on the curb.
Nobody wanted to comment on the broken chair in the corner.
Her train leaves on Thursday from the bus station.

notes: Probes: sitting / sit / sat / sits on 0.44-0.69; standing on 0.21, stood on 0.10, perched on 0.10, lying on 0.04, on Monday 0.03; 'sitting in' 0.12; 'do unto' 0.47. The - pole is ' along' / 'on board' after 'came' (arrival).
